newsitem.title: USA: Ohio corn, soybean seedings ahead of average pace.
newsitem.headline: Ohio corn, soybean seedings ahead of average pace.

text.p: Corn and soybean plantings in Ohio exceeded the average pace during the week ended Sunday, according to the Ohio Agricultural Statistiscs Service.
Corn plantings were 95 percent complete versus a five-year average of 78 percent and last year's pace of 35 percent.
Soybean plantings were 69 percent planted, compared with the average pace of 55 percent and last year's 12 percent, the report said.
Fifty-seven percent of the corn crop had emerged versus 21 percent last week. Twenty percent of the soybean crop had emerged compared to last week's figure of four percent.

Winter wheat was rated 10 percent excellent, 47 percent good, 30 percent fair, 10 percent poor and three percent very poor. Ninety-three percent of the wheat crop was jointed and two percent was headed.
Topsoil moisture levels were 19 percent surplus, 73 percent adequate and eight percent short.
